parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Lifecycle for a StyleMint.Modules.Networking.Entity.ConnectionIntroduction
(skill §7 IntroductionService surface).
            
State machine — all transitions out of Pending are terminal:
  Pending → AcceptedByA   (A acted → A→B request auto-sent)
  Pending → AcceptedByB   (B acted → B→A request auto-sent)
  Pending → Declined      (either A or B declined the intro)
  Pending → Expired       (60-day shelf-life sweeper, future phase)
            
First-action wins: once one side accepts, the intro is terminal
and the other side's UI surface is suppressed. Any attempt to
act on a terminal intro returns InvalidStateTransition so the
front-end can refresh.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description:
Per-vendor fulfillment lifecycle (skill §12). One SubOrder per vendor
inside an Order. State transitions are driven by:
  - payment events (Pending → Paid → AwaitingFulfillment)
  - vendor actions (AwaitingFulfillment → ReadyToShip → Shipped)
  - carrier-tracking events (Shipped → InTransit → OutForDelivery → Delivered)
  - cancel / return flows (any active state → Cancelled / Returned)
            

Customer Screen 23 (Track Order) renders a 6-node timeline:
Order Placed (= Pending) → Order Confirmed (= Paid/AwaitingFulfillment/
ReadyToShip/AwaitingTracking, collapsed) → Shipped → In Transit →
Out for Delivery → Delivered. The internal vendor-workflow states
(AwaitingFulfillment, ReadyToShip, AwaitingTracking) all map to the
same "Order Confirmed" node on the customer timeline.
Values 1-9 are stable for backward compatibility; the new
post-Shipped transit states are appended at 10 and 11 to avoid
renumbering existing DB rows.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description:
Lifecycle state of a Product. Per skill §9 + Q10 decision (Session 3):
soft-delete is via `Archived` only — there is no `is_deleted`
column on any Catalog entity.
            
State machine:
  Draft        → Active        (Publish)
  Active       → OutOfStock    (default variant exhausts inventory while
                                 TrackInventory=true and AllowOverselling=false)
  OutOfStock   → Active        (stock restored or AllowOverselling toggled on)
  Active|OutOfStock → Archived (soft-delete; vendor-initiated)
  Archived     → (terminal — re-listing creates a new Product row)
            
  Active|OutOfStock → Suspended           (admin-suspended owning vendor;
                                           reaction to Identity's
                                           AccountSuspendedV1 — see B11)
  Suspended         → Active              (vendor reinstated; reaction to
                                           AccountReinstatedV1)
            
`Suspended` hides the listing from public surfaces exactly like
`Archived`, but is reversible — the vendor's catalog comes back as
soon as the account is reinstated. Drafts owned by a suspended vendor
are left in Draft (not exposed publicly anyway).

Vendor §9G — bulk variant stock update on a single product.
Optional restock date + alert-customers flag travel through
the `catalog.product.stock-updated.v1` outbox event for
downstream Messaging (back-in-stock pushes).

soon as the account is reinstated. Drafts owned by a suspended vendor

Skill §2.1 — a candidate 3-second hook segment ranked by score.

StyleMint.Modules.CreatorStudio.Enums.Bo.description:

the window closes; Accepted moves the boost through stylemint-discovery's

  Active → Completed (target reel count reached), or → Dropped (creator

Terminal states are Completed and Dropped — no re-suggestion on the

StyleMint.Modules.Delivery.Entity.Packag.description:
Result of the NFC/Photo handoff endpoints (skill §6). Carries the
handshake state, the appended chain sequence (when applicable), and
the package's updated tracking state so the mobile client can
refresh the screen in one round-trip.

Module-internal projection of StyleMint.Modules.Delivery.Entity.Package.Package. Repositories return
this; controllers serialize it directly. RowVersion is base64-encoded for
safe round-tripping (HTTP headers).

StyleMint.Modules.Delivery.Enums.Deliver.description:
Closed set of exception codes a courier can report against a hop. The
canonical wire shape is the integer value; the string form is rendered
to buyers/vendors via Story Mode chapter copy.

Three-tier P2P delivery network (CLAUDE.md §1 Pillar B). Routing module
scores candidates per tier; this module persists the tier on the hop so
downstream surfaces (payouts, reputation, story-mode chapters) can render
tier-specific copy.

StyleMint.Modules.Delivery.Enums.HopStat.description:
Per-hop lifecycle (skill §2). State transitions are driven by courier
actions through `IHandoffService` (skill §6) and validated inside
StyleMint.Modules.Delivery.Entity.DeliveryHop.DeliveryHop methods.

StyleMint.Modules.Delivery.Enums.Package.description:
Lifecycle of a StyleMint.Modules.Delivery.Entity.Package.Package per skill §2.
Transitions are documented in skill §10 and enforced by entity methods.

StyleMint.Modules.Delivery.Enums.StoryCh.description:
Story Mode chapter classifier (skill §2). Presentation state — regenerable
from the chain of custody (skill §13 rule 7).

StyleMint.Modules.DeliveryCouriers.Enums.description:
Lifecycle of a `CourierProfile` aggregate (skill §2).
            
Allowed transitions:
  Applied → KycInReview → (Rejected | Onboarded)
  Onboarded → Active   (entered after the 30-day probation hop runs clean)
  Active   → Suspended (reliability-low / failure-streak / admin)
  Suspended → Active   (admin reinstate)
  * → Banned           (terminal admin action — no return path)

Three-tier delivery progression (strategy §3.7, skill §2). A profile holds
the highest tier they qualify for; routing tracks down (a Pro takes
Neighbor jobs too — checked at `stylemint-delivery-routing`).

Why the courier dropped a tier or was suspended (skill §3 + §11). Drives
the body of `delivery.courier.demoted.v1` / `suspended.v1` so
the courier sees the specific reason in their app.
State of a registered NFC / chain-of-custody signing key.

Reason the entry was written (skill §4). The append-only ledger lets the
running balance be derived deterministically from `SUM(amount * sign(kind))`.

Lifecycle of an individual escrow ledger row. `Held` is the steady
state for funds the courier deposited; `Released` for refunded
withdrawals; `Drawn` for admin-approved claim settlements.
State of a courier's submitted travel plan (skill §2).
Vehicle the courier carries packages on (skill §2).

currentGeohash.description: Geohash of the courier's currently-tracked position (or home for Neighbors).

rating.description: 0..5 customer/buyer rating; defaults to 3 (neutral) for new couriers.

providerHint.description: Optional pre-score sort hint (proximity for Pro, social distance for Neighbor, etc.).

recentDeclines24h.description: Recent decline count (last 24h) — feeds the recent_decline_penalty feature.

earningsLast7Days.description: Earnings in the last 7 days; lower → higher earnings_fairness boost.

travelPlanId.description:
Optional travel-plan id when the candidate is a Traveler — multi-hop
composition uses this to align middle-leg windows.

socialTrust.description: Optional social-trust score (0..1) for Neighbor candidates.

availableFromUtc.description: Optional ETA expressed as the courier's expected pickup window.

StyleMint.Modules.DeliveryRouting.Entity.description:
Skill §3 — a courier that *could* take the leg. Returned by the per-tier
candidate providers and consumed by the scorer. Treat as immutable.

Skill §6 — one leg in a single- or multi-hop route. StyleMint.Modules.DeliveryRouting.Entity.Routing.RoutingLeg.HopIndex
is zero-based; StyleMint.Modules.DeliveryRouting.Entity.Routing.RoutingLeg.HandoffGeohash is the geohash of the leg's
destination (the next leg's StyleMint.Modules.DeliveryRouting.Entity.Routing.RoutingLeg.OriginGeohash).

Skill §1 + §8 — the disposition of a single PlanAsync pass. Encapsulates
the eligibility decision, the resulting set of legs (1 for direct, up to 3
for multi-hop composition), the offer ids issued for the *first* leg
(subsequent legs are offered when the prior leg reaches handoff), and the
overall status.

Skill §4 — output of the delivery scorer. StyleMint.Modules.DeliveryRouting.Entity.Routing.ScoredCandidate.Score is the
weighted sum across all features; StyleMint.Modules.DeliveryRouting.Entity.Routing.ScoredCandidate.Breakdown retains the
per-feature contributions for transparent admin diagnostics.

Outcome of running the rule set against a package. StyleMint.Modules.DeliveryRouting.Entity.Routing.TierEligibilityResult.MatchedRule
is the first matching rule; the orchestrator logs it for forensic traceability.

StyleMint.Modules.DeliveryRouting.Enums..description:
Skill §12 — closed set of decline reasons. StyleMint.Modules.DeliveryRouting.Enums.DeclineReasonCode.Other requires
a free-text note (1..200 chars) supplied alongside the decline command.
Decline reasons feed the `recent_decline_penalty` scorer feature: a
courier with 3+ StyleMint.Modules.DeliveryRouting.Enums.DeclineReasonCode.TooFar declines in 24h gets a reduced
effective radius the next day.

Three-tier P2P delivery network (CLAUDE.md §1 Pillar B; skill §2).
Mirrors the same enum in stylemint-delivery and stylemint-delivery-couriers
— kept in-module so DeliveryRouting can compile without referencing the
other two delivery modules. Cross-module event payloads convert via the
shared underlying short value.

Skill §5. A HopOffer lives in exactly one state at a time. State machine:
  Pending → Accepted   (courier taps accept)
  Pending → Declined   (courier taps decline with reason)
  Pending → Expired    (90s window elapsed; sweeper)
  Pending → Superseded (a sibling offer in the same round was accepted first)
All terminal states are write-once. Acceptance of the winning offer flips
every other Pending offer for the same hop to Superseded inside the same
transaction (skill §13 rule 3).

Reasons the orchestrator re-plans a package mid-flight (skill §8 ReplanAsync).
Closed set; events carry the underlying short value for cross-module use.

Outcome of a routing pipeline pass (skill §1). Returned from
`IDeliveryOrchestrator.PlanAsync` so admin / dashboards can render
the high-level disposition without re-walking every offer row.

reasonCode.description: One of the closed report reason codes (SPAM / NUDITY_OR_SEXUAL / etc).

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Api.Controlle.description:
HTTP response for /v1/auth/login, /v1/auth/login-otp/verify,
/v1/auth/login-magic/consume, and /v1/auth/refresh. Same shape across
all four — every successful credential check yields an access+refresh bundle.

Logout the current session, or all sessions for the calling account.
AccountId is resolved by the controller from the authenticated principal,
not the request body — clients can't log other users out.

HTTP response for /v1/auth/login-otp/request. Plaintext code echoed
only when running under IHostEnvironment.IsDevelopment() — production
responses carry null. The code reaches users via the SMS/email channel
(Phase B1/B2 delivery, currently dev-only logged).

HTTP shape returned by POST /v1/auth/password-reset/request. Always 200
regardless of whether the email is on file — anti-enumeration.
StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Api.Controllers.V1.ViewModels.Auth.PasswordResetRequestedVm.DevPlaintextToken echoed only in Development for client
convenience; in production it is omitted.
Callback-step payload — provider returns code + state to the client; client posts both here.
Authorize-step payload — the caller's redirect URI.

HTTP response shape for POST /v1/otp. Intentionally omits the plaintext code —
the code travels via the messaging module (email/SMS) not the HTTP response body.

Request body for `POST /v1/auth/passkeys/register/bootstrap/complete`:
completes the WebAuthn registration started by bootstrap/options and issues
a session. The device is ensured-or-created from StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Api.Controllers.V1.ViewModels.Passkey.BootstrapCompleteVm.DeviceFingerprint
(a fresh install has no per-account device id yet).

Request body for `POST /v1/auth/passkeys/register/bootstrap/options` —
passkey-first signup. Only a display name is required; email/phone are
collected later (progressive onboarding).

Response for `POST /v1/auth/passkeys/register/bootstrap/options`: the
newly-created account id plus the WebAuthn registration challenge. The
client creates the credential and posts back to bootstrap/complete.

Web client request to begin a QR login. The browser supplies a stable
device fingerprint (e.g. persisted in localStorage); the minted session is
bound to it.

Response to POST /v1/auth/qr/exchange. StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Api.Controllers.V1.ViewModels.QrLogin.QrExchangeResponseVm.Status is the session
state ("Pending"/"Scanned"/"Approved"/"Consumed"/"Rejected"/"Expired").
StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Api.Controllers.V1.ViewModels.QrLogin.QrExchangeResponseVm.Auth is populated exactly once, when Status becomes "Consumed".
Web poll request: exchange an approved QR session for tokens.

Response to POST /v1/auth/qr/create. The web renders StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Api.Controllers.V1.ViewModels.QrLogin.QrLoginCreatedVm.QrPayload
as a QR code and keeps StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Api.Controllers.V1.ViewModels.QrLogin.QrLoginCreatedVm.ClientSecret privately (never in the QR),
presenting it on exchange. StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Api.Controllers.V1.ViewModels.QrLogin.QrLoginCreatedVm.PublicToken identifies the session.

Response to POST /v1/auth/qr/{publicToken}/scan — what the mobile shows on
its "Approve this login?" confirmation screen.

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.Account.description:
Per skill rule 19 — account deletion has a 30-day grace period. Pending requests are
reversible by the user up until ExecuteAtUtc; after that the worker job flips to
Executed and the data is purged.

Account lifecycle state. Values are explicit per CLAUDE.md invariant #14.
Transitions (Day 1 scope):
  Active      → Suspended  (admin Suspend)
  Suspended   → Active     (admin Reinstate)
Additional transitions (Deactivate/Delete/Purge) land with GDPR work in later weeks.

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.BlockSc.description:
Surface that a block applies to. `All` hides the blocker from EVERY surface
the blocked user could see; narrower scopes block specific interaction types.
Different from Networking module's mutual-friendship blocks — this is one-way and
surface-specific.

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.Busines.description:
Legal form of a vendor entity. Determines which fields on `vendor_profiles` are
required (e.g. `BusinessRegistrationNumber` is mandatory for non-Individual forms)
and drives downstream tax-information capture (Week 4).

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.Consent.description:
Categories of legally-required consent receipts (§9 + GDPR).
Values are append-only — existing records keep their consent type forever.

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.DataAcc.description:
What the actor did with the data. `View` is the common case; `Export` /
`Download` are the heavy-access cases that SAR responses call out in the
"these exports have been produced" section.

Who accessed the data. Self-access (the user reading their own profile) is NOT logged
here — it's the default browse path and would flood the table. We only log when
someone OTHER than the subject touches the subject's data.

GDPR data-category buckets for Subject Access Request accounting. The category on each
row tells the SAR export what section it lands in; the set is deliberately coarse (8
buckets, not hundreds of field-level categories) so the audit stays readable.

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.DataRig.description:
State machine for a data-rights request. GDPR caps response time at 30 days
(extendable by 60 days for complex cases) — tracked via DueAtUtc on the entity.

GDPR Articles 15-22 surface for data subject rights. The user picks one when filing a
request; downstream workers handle each type differently (Export = render+ship a zip,
Erasure = trigger AccountDeletionRequest, Correction = open a support ticket, etc.).

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.DeviceA.description:
Which mobile attestation framework produced the assertion. Distinct from
StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.DevicePlatform — that one is the device's OS family; this one is the
specific attestation provider whose payload we verified.

Outcome of verifying an attestation payload against the platform's PKI / API.
Every row is recorded — failures are the load-bearing input for fraud scoring.

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.DeviceP.description:
Device operating system / runtime platform. One of a fixed set; values are explicit
per CLAUDE.md invariant on enums. Unknown is the catch-all for non-first-party clients
(test harnesses, scripts) so device registration never fails on an unrecognized UA.

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.DeviceT.description:
Trust posture for a device. Untrusted on first registration; promoted to Trusted
after the user confirms via a step-up check (email/phone code) on that device.
Revoked is terminal — a new registration of the same fingerprint starts a new row.

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.Externa.description:
Social-login providers we accept. Per CLAUDE.md §6 the locked v2.0 set is Google,
Apple, Facebook. Twitter/X is NOT supported (it's also excluded from Pillar E).

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.KycRisk.description:
Risk tier the KYC reviewer assigned. Drives downstream limits — e.g. Elevated tier
caps wallet balance, requires manual review on payouts above a threshold.

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.KycSess.description:
Session-level KYC state.
  - Pending     : created, awaiting user document upload
  - Submitted   : user uploaded all required docs, awaiting review
  - UnderReview : admin / provider is actively reviewing
  - Approved    : terminal — KYC passed
  - Rejected    : terminal — KYC failed (reason captured)
  - Expired     : terminal — session timed out without submission

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.Lockout.description:
Why an account was locked. `BruteForce` is the automatic detection from
`login_attempts` aggregates; `MaxMfaFailures` is the MFA-challenge analog.
`AdminLock` and `FraudDetected` are system/admin-initiated with indefinite
duration (no UnlockAtUtc) until manually lifted.

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.LoginId.description:
How the user presented themselves for login. The raw identifier is hashed before being
stored on `login_attempts.identifier_hash` so logs don't leak PII.

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.LoginMe.description:
Which credential the login attempt presented. Must be logged even when it fails
per §9 rule 13 — e.g. "attempted password login against a passwordless account".

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.LoginOu.description:
Result of a login attempt. Every outcome is persisted append-only per §9 rule 13 —
failures and rate-limited attempts are the primary input to lockout + risk scoring.

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.MagicLi.description:
What a magic link, when clicked, authorizes the bearer to do. Each purpose has slightly
different semantics downstream — `Login` issues a session, `EmailVerification`
flips `AccountEmail.VerifiedUtc`, `PasswordReset` opens a short-lived reset
window that the UI uses to POST a new password without the current one.

Magic-link lifecycle. Active is the only usable state. Consumed (one-time click
redeemed) and Expired (beyond `ExpiresUtc` — typically materialized by sweep job)
and Invalidated (superseded — e.g. a fresh link for the same purpose was issued) are
all terminal. A presented link whose row is non-Active MUST be rejected without
leaking why (to avoid link-enumeration or timing signals).

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.Marketi.description:
GDPR-scoped marketing consent buckets. Separate from transactional messaging (order
confirmations, security alerts) — those are governed by `notification_preferences`,
not marketing consent, because they're operationally necessary.

Where the user's grant/withdraw decision was captured. GDPR review needs an auditable
trail to prove an "Onboarding" opt-in wasn't pre-ticked or a settings toggle wasn't
flipped by a background job.

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.Message.description:
Who may initiate a direct message to this account. Default is FriendsOnly per
safety-by-default stance — unsolicited DMs from strangers are the #1 abuse vector.

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.MfaMeth.description:
MFA enrollment lifecycle.
  - Pending: user started enrollment but has not yet verified one code against the
    method. An enroll is not considered a valid second factor at login until Active.
  - Active: verified at least once; eligible to be challenged at login.
  - Disabled: removed by user or admin. Terminal for this row; a fresh enroll of the
    same destination starts a new row.

Supported second-factor methods. TOTP stores an encrypted secret on the row; SMS/Email
store only a SHA-256 hash of the destination so logs never leak raw phone/email.
Passkey is NOT a second factor — passkeys are their own primary method; a user enrolled
in a passkey is already "MFA-grade" and doesn't need another row here.

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.Payment.description:
Locked v1.1 spec — exactly four payment methods. No Stripe-as-method, no Khalti.
Stripe / Adyen sit BEHIND `VisaMastercard` as the underlying processor; the user
sees "Visa/Mastercard" in the UI regardless of which gateway routes the charge.

Per-instrument lifecycle. Active is the only state that can be charged. Expired is set
either by the sweep job past the captured expiry or by a webhook from the processor.
Removed is user-initiated termination; ProcessorRevoked is processor-initiated.

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.PayoutM.description:
Locked v1.1 spec — exactly four payout destinations. New methods need both an
architecture decision and a sanctions-screening update before extending.

Per skill rule 14 — adding a payout method requires sanctions / PEP screening to
pass before the row goes Active. New rows ship as PendingScreening; the screening
service flips them to Active or Rejected.

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.Profile.description:
Review state for a Creator- or Vendor-profile application. Mirrors the 1–3 business-day
SLA in the onboarding skill. Pending on submit; Approved flips the corresponding
`role_profiles` row to Active; Rejected keeps the RoleProfile in Pending and carries
a reason so the user can re-apply after addressing feedback.

Who can see a user's profile page / bio / avatar. Default is Public — the platform is
fundamentally social-commerce, so accounts ship discoverable unless the user opts down.

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.QrLogin.description:
Which web studio a QR login session targets. Drives role gating on approval:
BrandStudio requires an active Vendor role-profile; CreatorStudio requires an
active Creator role-profile. Values are explicit per the CLAUDE.md enum invariant.

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.Recover.description:
Individual recovery-code row lifecycle. Active is the only usable state. Consumed
(redeemed at login) and Revoked (batch invalidated by regen) are both terminal — a
code transitioning out of Active cannot come back.

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.RoleTyp.description:
Role assumed by an Account. One human = one Account = many role-profiles.
Used by account_handles (ContextRole), role_profiles (Week 2+), and other modules
that need to know which role-view to show.

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.SearchV.description:
Whether the account appears in search/discovery. `Hidden` means the handle can only
be reached via direct link — never surfaced through discovery, feed recommendations, or
"people you may know." Different from StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.ProfileVisibility: profile may be
Private while still being findable by handle, and vice-versa.

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.Securit.description:
UI-facing severity for a security event. Critical rows trigger the "security alert"
push notification per §9 rule 12 (token reuse, suspicious sign-in) regardless of the
user's notification preferences — they're transactional security, not marketing.

Categories for the user-visible security timeline. The set is stable — add new values
but never reshuffle existing ones (historical rows keep their type forever).

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.Session.description:
Why a session was revoked. Recorded alongside `RevokedUtc` for forensic /
security-timeline UX. `TokenReuseDetected` is the sentinel that triggers §9 rule 12
(revoke the entire refresh-token chain + raise a Critical RiskSignal).

UserSession lifecycle. Active is the only status that allows token rotation;
Revoked (explicit sign-out / compromise) and Expired (beyond the refresh window)
are both terminal. Status is decided at read time by the service using `ExpiresUtc`
+ `RevokedUtc`; Active rows never need to be rewritten merely because time moved on.

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.TaxForm.description:
Tax form attestation types. US persons submit W-9; non-US individuals W-8BEN; non-US
entities W-8BEN-E. Local equivalents (PAN/TPIN for Nepal, GSTIN for India) round out
the set so the platform can issue payouts compliantly across markets.

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.VendorT.description:
A team member's authority within a vendor account.
  - `Owner`: exactly one per vendor. Can manage billing, transfer ownership, delete.
  - `Admin`: can invite/remove non-Owner members, manage products, view reports.
  - `Member`: day-to-day operations (manage listings, fulfill orders), no org-level changes.

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.Verific.description:
Which side of a multi-side document this row represents. Single-side documents
(passport, selfie, address proof) use StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.VerificationDocumentSide.NotApplicable.

Per-document review state. `Uploaded` is the post-upload pre-review state;
`UnderReview` means an admin / KYC provider has it; terminal Approved/Rejected.

Government-issued identity document type. Each type has known sides
(passport = single page; ID card / driver's license = front + back).

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.WalletS.description:
Wallet lifecycle. Frozen blocks all debit/credit operations (used for fraud holds);
Closed is terminal — the row stays for audit but balance must be zero before closing.

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.WalletT.description:
Which module / flow originated a wallet transaction. Powers the user-visible
"Transaction history" filters and the cross-module reconciliation reports.

Per-row classification of a wallet ledger entry. Per skill rule 15 the ledger is
APPEND-ONLY — reversals append a new row with `ReversalOf` set on the
transaction entity, never UPDATE the original.

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Service.Magic.description:
Returned on successful consume so the caller can route the user into the right
post-consume flow (issue a session for Login, flip VerifiedUtc for EmailVerification,
open a password-reset window for PasswordReset).

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Service.OAuth.description: Authorize-step response — the URL the mobile client redirects the user to.

Callback-step response — resolved provider profile + flag for
whether the caller needs to issue a real JWT next. Day-1 the JWT
minting is left to a follow-up; the controller surfaces enough
info that the mobile client can recover the session via existing
password / OTP flows in the interim.

StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Service.Regis.description:
Snapshot of an account's registration progress. Returned from
M:StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Service.RegistrationService.IRegistrationService.AcceptTermsAsync(StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Service.RegistrationService.Commands.AcceptTermsCommand,System.Threading.CancellationToken) as the final-step
payload so the caller has a single round-trip's worth of state to render.
            
`IsComplete` = email verified AND phone verified AND terms accepted AND
(has password OR has passkey) — the canonical "registration done" check per
session-1 decision 1b (no AccountStatus.Pending; completion is derived).
A passkey-only account (no password) is valid.

Result of M:StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Service.RegistrationService.IRegistrationService.StartAsync(StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Service.RegistrationService.Commands.StartRegistrationCommand,System.Threading.CancellationToken). Carries the
account/email/phone ids the client needs for the subsequent verify steps,
the OTP expiries (so the client can show countdowns), and — only when the
service is running in Development — the OTP plaintexts. Production builds
receive `null` for the two code fields; the codes are delivered out
of band via the Messaging module.
            
`Resumed` is true when StartAsync found an existing account for the
provided email and reused it instead of registering fresh. This signal
lets the client distinguish "first time on this device" from "retry of
an earlier attempt", which matters for analytics and for messages like
"we sent a fresh code to your inbox" vs. "welcome back".

StyleMint.Modules.Matchmaking.Api.Contro.description:
Optional reviewer note attached to an Approve decision (skill
§4.4 — admins capture rationale for the audit trail).

Mandatory rejection rationale — captured so future-self can see
why a high-fit pair was killed by curation (skill §4.4).

passed.description: True when every StyleMint.Modules.Matchmaking.Entity.FairnessAuditReport.Dtos.FairnessAuditReportDto.Axes entry passes the ±0.2 parity bound.

maxDisparityIndex.description: Worst-case disparity across all axes — drives the gating decision.

axes.description: Per-axis breakdown for the published report.

StyleMint.Modules.Matchmaking.Entity.Fai.description:
Outcome of one quarterly fairness audit (skill §13.3). The audit
computes disparity-index ratios across tracked demographic axes
(region, language, creator-age bucket, brand-size bucket — never
protected-class attributes). A run "passes" when every axis sits
within ±0.2 of parity (disparity index in [0.83, 1.20]).

StyleMint.Modules.Matchmaking.Enums.Feat.description:
Lifecycle of a StyleMint.Modules.Matchmaking.Entity.FeaturedMatchCandidate.FeaturedMatchCandidate
in the weekly curation queue (skill §4.4).
            
State machine:
  PendingReview → Approved   (admin accepts)
  PendingReview → Rejected   (admin declines)
  Approved      → Pushed     (notification delivered to both sides)
  Pushed        → Acted      (match turned into a partnership)
            
Skill §13 rule 7 — Featured matches always go through admin review;
the platform never auto-pushes a curated match.

StyleMint.Modules.Matchmaking.Enums.Matc.description:
Where a StyleMint.Modules.Matchmaking.Entity.MatchSnapshot.MatchSnapshot came from.
Drives the per-pair uniqueness constraint (skill §13 rule 10) and
the read-path indexes — daily-creator and daily-brand lists are the
two hot surfaces.

Lifecycle state of a StyleMint.Modules.Matchmaking.Entity.MatchSnapshot.MatchSnapshot.
StyleMint.Modules.Matchmaking.Enums.MatchSnapshotState.Surfaced is the only state that appears on the daily
list reads; the others are terminal and filtered out.
            
State machine:
  Surfaced → ActedOn               (invite / proposal sent)
  Surfaced → DismissedByCreator    (creator tapped dismiss)
  Surfaced → DismissedByBrand      (brand tapped dismiss)
  Surfaced → Expired               (nightly recompute superseded)
            
Skill §13 rule 5 — dismissals are sticky; the same counterparty
must not re-surface after either side dismisses.

matchSnapshotId.description: The originating match — used by stylemint-partnerships to mark `MatchSnapshot.State` ActedOn on invite creation.

proposedCommissionBps.description: Score-linear commission proposal in basis points (skill §6 formula), clamped to the brand's range.

matchScore.description: Score that drove the proposal — used by the screen to show "high match → higher rate" context.

reasonSummary.description: Plain-language top-3 reasons carried forward from the snapshot.

brandBriefId.description:
Latest `Locked` brand brief identifier from stylemint-brand-studio,
or null when the brand has no brief yet (the partnership UI then
falls back to a blank brief). Populated by the cross-module reader.

StyleMint.Modules.Matchmaking.Service.Pa.description:
Pre-filled fields for the one-tap partnership invite (skill §6).
Both sides see the same prefill; either side can edit before
committing — the partnerships module owns the final invite
payload.

apnsId.description: apns-id we recorded as ProviderMessageId at send time.

unregisteredToken.description: Device token if APNs marks it stale.

StyleMint.Modules.Messaging.Api.Controll.description:
APNs HTTP/2 delivery feedback. APNs doesn't push receipts; this
endpoint is fed by a bridge that polls the APNs "feedback" channel
or by an internal job that retries based on HTTP/2 response codes.

messageId.description: FCM message id we recorded as ProviderMessageId at send time.

errorCode.description: Provider error code on failure; empty on success.

unregisteredToken.description: Optional — present when the failure indicates a dead token.

StyleMint.Modules.Messaging.Api.Controll.description:
Receipt body posted by an FCM delivery / failure callback bridge.
The native FCM API doesn't push receipts directly — most setups route
receipts through Cloud Pub/Sub → Cloud Functions → this endpoint.
Bridge service shapes the body into this minimal form.

Message.description: Stringified SES notification JSON; deserialize separately.

StyleMint.Modules.Messaging.Api.Controll.description:
SNS-wrapped SES bounce / complaint / delivery notification.
AWS posts SNS messages where StyleMint.Modules.Messaging.Api.Controllers.V1.ViewModels.Webhooks.SesSnsMessageVm.Message is a stringified
JSON document with the SES payload. The Type field discriminates
SubscriptionConfirmation vs Notification.
            
Production deployments should also verify the SNS message signature
using SigningCertURL — that lives behind an
`ISnsMessageSignatureVerifier` abstraction (not in v1).

StyleMint.Modules.Messaging.Enums.Device.description:
Push token target platform for a registered device.
Drives which adapter (FCM vs APNs) handles delivery.

StyleMint.Modules.Messaging.Enums.Messag.description:
Conversation context — drives what participants are allowed and
what UI surface renders the thread. v1 supports the two needed
for the screens: VendorCreatorPartnership (Vendor §7N, Creator
§7I), and CreatorBrandPartnership (mirror view for the brand).

phoneHashes.description:
SHA-256 hex strings produced client-side per skill §6.
Server NEVER stores these; they're discarded after the
resolution pass.

redemptionCap.description: Optional global redemption cap. Null = unlimited.

code.description: 10-char Crockford base32 code the redeemer was given.

StyleMint.Modules.Networking.Entity.Dtos.description:
Anonymous-safe projection used by the by-code lookup on the
signup page. Deliberately omits redemption counts, caps, and
other inviter-private fields — the prospective signer-up only
needs to know whose invite this is + whether it's still good.

StyleMint.Modules.Networking.Enums.Block.description:
Why the blocker blocked (skill §7 BlockReason enum). Stored for
moderation analytics + admin review; deliberately NOT included
in the StyleMint.Modules.Networking.Events.ConnectionBlockedV1
payload so the reason doesn't ride across the wire to consumer
modules that don't need it (Identity mirror, Messaging gate).

StyleMint.Modules.Networking.Enums.Conne.description:
The built-in friend-category set (skill §4) plus a `Custom`
escape hatch for user-defined labels. A user can place a friend
in any number of categories simultaneously — Close Friends AND a
Custom "Book Club" tag are both valid.
            
Categories are PRIVATE per side (skill §4 last line): A's
categorization of B is invisible to B and never exposed via
integration events.

Lifecycle for a StyleMint.Modules.Networking.Entity.ConnectionIntroduction
(skill §7 IntroductionService surface).
            
State machine — all transitions out of Pending are terminal:
  Pending → AcceptedByA   (A acted → A→B request auto-sent)
  Pending → AcceptedByB   (B acted → B→A request auto-sent)
  Pending → Declined      (either A or B declined the intro)
  Pending → Expired       (60-day shelf-life sweeper, future phase)
            
First-action wins: once one side accepts, the intro is terminal
and the other side's UI surface is suppressed. Any attempt to
act on a terminal intro returns InvalidStateTransition so the
front-end can refresh.

Lifecycle states for a StyleMint.Modules.Networking.Entity.ConnectionRequest
(skill §3). Stored as SMALLINT; integer values are wire-stable.
            
Terminal states: StyleMint.Modules.Networking.Enums.ConnectionRequestStatus.Accepted, StyleMint.Modules.Networking.Enums.ConnectionRequestStatus.Declined,
StyleMint.Modules.Networking.Enums.ConnectionRequestStatus.Expired, StyleMint.Modules.Networking.Enums.ConnectionRequestStatus.Withdrawn. Only
StyleMint.Modules.Networking.Enums.ConnectionRequestStatus.Pending permits an action.

StyleMint.Modules.Networking.Enums.Conta.description:
Lifecycle for a StyleMint.Modules.Networking.Entity.ContactImport. `Active`
while the import's matches are surfaced to the customer;
`Deleted` on user-initiated tear-down (skill §6 privacy:
the user can wipe their import history any time). The row stays
for forensic audit but matches are physically deleted when the
import flips to `Deleted`.

StyleMint.Modules.Networking.Enums.Invit.description:
Persisted lifecycle for an StyleMint.Modules.Networking.Entity.InviteLink.
`Expired` is NOT in this enum — expiry is computed against
`ExpiresUtc` at query/use time so a single sweeper isn't
required to keep the column accurate. The three values cover
admin/user-initiated state changes only.

StyleMint.Modules.Networking.Enums.PymkR.description:
Why the PYMK service suggested this candidate (skill §5 +
skill §7 PymkReason enum). v1 only lights up
StyleMint.Modules.Networking.Enums.PymkReason.FriendsOfFriends; the rest of the alphabet is
reserved for the corresponding cross-module signal sources
(contact match → N6 ContactMatches; same profession/location →
Identity mirror; mutual group → Community module).

StyleMint.Modules.Networking.Enums.PymkS.description:
Lifecycle for a StyleMint.Modules.Networking.Entity.PymkSuggestion.
`Dismissed` is temporary — skill §5 specifies a 90-day
cooldown, tracked via `DismissedUntilUtc`. The next
recompute pass flips the row back to StyleMint.Modules.Networking.Enums.PymkSuggestionStatus.Active
when the cooldown lapses (unless the candidate was meanwhile
marked StyleMint.Modules.Networking.Enums.PymkSuggestionStatus.Uninteresting, which is permanent).

StyleMint.Modules.Onboarding.Entity.Dtos.description:
API-safe view of the vendor application bank account: full routing /
account numbers stay server-side, only the last four account digits
surface here so a leaked DTO doesn't expose the full number.

StyleMint.Modules.Onboarding.Enums.Appli.description:
Lifecycle of a CreatorApplication / VendorApplication. Per skill §9:
  Draft → Submitted → UnderReview → Approved | Rejected.
Values are explicit per CLAUDE.md invariant 14.

StyleMint.Modules.Onboarding.Enums.Audie.description:
Self-reported follower count band on a CreatorApplication. Bands match
the Figma "Audience size" picker chips. Skill §3 references the value
without enumerating; this set is the canonical Day-1 list and is
admin-extensible later via configuration.

StyleMint.Modules.Onboarding.Enums.BankA.description:
Bank-account type captured on the application form (Vendor Screen 1D).
Stored as smallint at the DB level; mapped to processor-specific
values during post-approval promotion to Identity's payout method.

StyleMint.Modules.Onboarding.Enums.Busin.description:
Legal form of the vendor entity, captured at application time and passed to
Identity's `VendorProfile` on approval. Mirrors the values of
`StyleMint.Modules.Identity.Enums.BusinessType`; per the architecture
rule that modules don't share enums across boundaries, Onboarding owns its
own copy and the approval composer maps int-to-int.

StyleMint.Modules.Onboarding.Enums.Catal.description:
Vendor's self-reported estimate of catalog size, captured on the
application form (Vendor Screen 1E — Product Information dropdown).
Used by matchmaking to bucket vendors into peer cohorts and by ops
to size onboarding support; never authoritative against the actual
product count post-approval.

StyleMint.Modules.Onboarding.Enums.Socia.description:
External platforms a creator can declare as their public presence on the
Creator Application. Matches the four platforms Style Mint supports
across Reels / Reach (per CLAUDE.md §3 platform list — Twitter/X excluded).

StyleMint.Modules.Onboarding.Enums.Vendo.description:
Typed list of vendor-application KYC documents. Mirrors the four
upload slots on Vendor Screen 1C — Business Documents step. The
first three are required; StyleMint.Modules.Onboarding.Enums.VendorApplicationDocumentKind.CertificateOfIncorporation
is optional. StyleMint.Modules.Onboarding.Enums.VendorApplicationDocumentKind.Other exists so jurisdictions outside the
US/Nepal launch set can attach supplementary docs without a code
change.

StyleMint.Modules.Orders.Api.Controllers.description:
Request body for `POST /v1/orders/{orderNumber}/cancel`.
SubOrderId null = whole-order cancel; set = partial (per-vendor)
cancel. Note required only when Reason == Other (skill §13.5).

photoUrls.description:
At least one URL required (skill §13.7). Uploaded out-of-band
through the media module; we store URL references only.

StyleMint.Modules.Orders.Api.Controllers.description:
Request body for `POST /v1/orders/{orderNumber}/returns`
per skill §5. AccountId resolved from JWT — never accepted from the wire.

Shared payload for the two §3B–3C bulk fulfillment endpoints:
"Mark Multiple as Shipped" and "Print All Packing Slips". Both
consume a list of sub-order ids; both reply with a
`BulkResult<T>` reporting per-row outcomes.

StyleMint.Modules.Orders.Entity.Dtos.Ord.description:
Customer-facing order detail (skill §9). Returned by the
`GET /v1/orders/{orderNumber}` endpoint. Denormalized so a
single round-trip renders the entire Order Details screen
(CLAUDE.md §3, mobile-first).

Customer §25 invoice projection. Mirrors the on-screen invoice
layout so the mobile client can render Save / Print without
reshaping StyleMint.Modules.Orders.Entity.Dtos.OrderDto. Shipping address is denormalised
from the order snapshot; creator commission rolls up across lines.

Lightweight summary for the customer's order list. Mobile-first
shape — denormalized so the My Orders screen renders without a
follow-up call: order number, state, total, vendor count, item
count, and a single thumbnail for the visual cue.

StyleMint.Modules.Orders.Entity.Dtos.Pac.description:
Vendor §3D Print Packing Slip projection. Server returns the
structured payload — the mobile client (or admin web console)
renders the PDF / printer-friendly view off this DTO so a future
server-side PDF generator can plug in without changing the
contract.

StyleMint.Modules.Orders.Entity.Dtos.Ret.description:
Returned by `POST /v1/orders/{orderNumber}/returns`. The customer
app uses this to render the "return submitted" screen and link to the
auto-opened support ticket (looked up via Support's
`ReturnRequestId` filter).

StyleMint.Modules.Orders.Entity.Dtos.Ven.description:
Per-creator sales performance for one vendor over a time window — how much
each creator's reel-tagged lines sold of this vendor's products, and the
commission the vendor paid that creator. Derived entirely from
`SubOrderLine` attribution (CreatorAccountId / CommissionAmount /
OriginatingReelId); no cross-module join. Ordered by attributed revenue desc.

Vendor-scoped sub-order detail (skill §9, ticket SM-BG-2). The list row
(StyleMint.Modules.Orders.Entity.Dtos.VendorSubOrderListItemDto) intentionally omits the heavy
parts; this is the full shape the vendor order-detail screen needs in one
round-trip: the parent order number + placement time, the
StyleMint.Modules.Orders.Entity.Dtos.VendorSubOrderDetailDto.ShipTo snapshot (including receiver name for the customer
label), the fulfillment lifecycle fields, totals, and the line items.
            
Ownership is enforced in the service: a sub-order owned by another vendor
surfaces as NotFound (never 403) so cross-vendor ids aren't leaked.

Vendor's pending-fulfillment row (skill §9 GET /v1/vendor/sub-orders).
Denormalizes order number + customer-facing total so the dashboard
renders without a follow-up call. The Lines + ShipTo live on the
detailed shape — vendors use the customer's existing
/v1/orders/{number} for that today; a vendor-scoped detail endpoint
can ship later if needed.

StyleMint.Modules.Orders.Enums.OrderCanc.description:
Customer-facing cancel reason taxonomy (skill §4). Closed set —
the mobile UI shows exactly these six options. StyleMint.Modules.Orders.Enums.OrderCancellationReason.Other
requires a free-text note (1..500 chars) on the request.

StyleMint.Modules.Orders.Enums.OrderStat.description:
Customer-facing order lifecycle (skill §12). Cascades to SubOrder
transitions on payment + delivery events.
            
  Placed     → Paid          (payments.intent.succeeded.v1)
  Placed     → Cancelled     (cancel before payment)
  Paid       → Fulfilling    (any SubOrder ships)
  Paid       → Cancelled     (cancel approved, full order)
  Fulfilling → Completed     (all SubOrders delivered)
            
Completed / Cancelled are terminal.

StyleMint.Modules.Orders.Enums.ReturnReq.description:
State machine for StyleMint.Modules.Orders.Entity.ReturnRequest per skill §5.
            
  Submitted ─► Approved ─► Completed
       │
       └─► Rejected
            
Completed is the only state that flips the parent SubOrder to
StyleMint.Modules.Orders.Enums.SubOrderState.Returned and publishes
`orders.sub_order.returned.v1`. Rejected is terminal.

StyleMint.Modules.Orders.Enums.SubOrderS.description:
Per-vendor fulfillment lifecycle (skill §12). One SubOrder per vendor
inside an Order. State transitions are driven by:
  - payment events (Pending → Paid → AwaitingFulfillment)
  - vendor actions (AwaitingFulfillment → ReadyToShip → Shipped)
  - carrier-tracking events (Shipped → InTransit → OutForDelivery → Delivered)
  - cancel / return flows (any active state → Cancelled / Returned)
            

Customer Screen 23 (Track Order) renders a 6-node timeline:
Order Placed (= Pending) → Order Confirmed (= Paid/AwaitingFulfillment/
ReadyToShip/AwaitingTracking, collapsed) → Shipped → In Transit →
Out for Delivery → Delivered. The internal vendor-workflow states
(AwaitingFulfillment, ReadyToShip, AwaitingTracking) all map to the
same "Order Confirmed" node on the customer timeline.
Values 1-9 are stable for backward compatibility; the new
post-Shipped transit states are appended at 10 and 11 to avoid
renumbering existing DB rows.

StyleMint.Modules.Partnerships.Api.Contr.description:
HTTP payload mirror of `TermsBody`. We keep a separate VM here so
the API contract is decoupled from the entity's serialization shape.

StyleMint.Modules.Partnerships.Entity.Pa.description:
One row in the §7J "Search creators to invite" picker. Display
fields come from Identity's `CreatorProfile`; the
StyleMint.Modules.Partnerships.Entity.Partnership.Dtos.CreatorPickerDto.HasExistingPartnership flag is computed in the
service against this vendor's partnership list so the picker can
dim or filter out creators the vendor is already working with.

Read projection of a StyleMint.Modules.Partnerships.Entity.Partnership.Partnership. Carries the joined
vendor rating (sourced from `stylemint-catalog` via
`IVendorRatingProvider`) so the mobile brand-detail view ships
in one round-trip (CLAUDE.md §3 — mobile-first API shape).

Skill §6 — projection at 50 sales for the "Potential Earnings" screen.
StyleMint.Modules.Partnerships.Entity.Partnership.Dtos.PotentialEarningsDto.CommissionRate is the midpoint of the partnership's
commission range (v1.1 doesn't pin per-product rates).

Read projection of a StyleMint.Modules.Partnerships.Entity.PartnershipTermsVersion.PartnershipTermsVersion. The
structured body is hydrated from JSONB into the typed
StyleMint.Modules.Partnerships.Entity.PartnershipTermsVersion.TermsBody shape so the mobile renderer doesn't have to
parse JSON itself.

length.description:
Half-open length of the link range. `EndIndex` is exclusive
so an empty range (Start == End) is invalid by construction.

StyleMint.Modules.Partnerships.Entity.Pa.description:
Skill §2 + §12 rule 5 — inline anchor inside a bullet. We store offsets
into the bullet text instead of embedding markup so:
  - the mobile renderer can walk the bullet without parsing,
  - link metadata roundtrips through JSON cleanly,
  - overlapping or out-of-range ranges fail fast at publish time.
            
Immutable value object; equality is structural.

Skill §2 — a single bullet inside the Reel Content Rules section.
Holds the rendered text plus zero or more StyleMint.Modules.Partnerships.Entity.PartnershipTermsVersion.InlineLink
offsets pointing into that text.

Skill §2 — "Reel Content Rules" section. Bullets carry inline-link
offsets; each bullet validates its own ranges (see
M:StyleMint.Modules.Partnerships.Entity.PartnershipTermsVersion.ReelContentRuleBullet.Validate(System.Int32)).

Skill §4 — the structured terms body is persisted as a single JSONB
column (`body`). This wrapper provides the canonical serializer
settings used by the EF value converter on the entity, the publish
service, and the unit tests. Centralising the settings means schema
changes (adding sections in v2.1+) don't drift between read and write
paths.

Skill §2 — "Who Can Join" section. Plain-bullet structure (no inline
links per skill spec) — gating conditions like minimum followers,
content categories, geography.

StyleMint.Modules.Partnerships.Enums.Par.description:
Skill §2 + §11 — 5-state machine for the Partnership aggregate.
Transitions:
  Invited → Active           (Creator accepts)
  Invited → Declined         (Creator declines; terminal)
  Active  → Paused           (Vendor pauses)
  Paused  → Active           (Vendor resumes)
  Active  | Paused → Ended   (Vendor ends, or catalog.vendor.deactivated.v1)
            
Only StyleMint.Modules.Partnerships.Enums.PartnershipState.Active partnerships may be referenced from new
reel tags (skill §12 rule 7). Existing tagged reels keep earning
through their commission snapshot when the partnership is Paused.

label.description: Customer-typed label. Null or empty clears it.

StyleMint.Modules.Payments.Api.Controlle.description:
Shared payload for the three webhook endpoints. The mobile / PSP
pre-parses the provider's payload into this shared shape — the
service layer doesn't need to know each provider's vocabulary.

displayLast4.description: Last 4 PAN digits — display only, not PCI-sensitive.

StyleMint.Modules.Payments.Enums.SavedPa.description:
Lifecycle for a StyleMint.Modules.Payments.Entity.SavedPaymentMethod. `Removed`
is a soft-delete — historical StyleMint.Modules.Payments.Entity.PaymentIntent rows
may carry the saved-method id forward, so we keep the row but exclude
it from list responses and refuse new uses.

StyleMint.Modules.Payments.Service.Payme.description:
Outcome the provider's payload is signaling about the intent —
the controller pre-parses the provider-specific status code into
this shared shape so the service can apply the right transition
without knowing each provider's vocabulary.

StyleMint.Modules.Payouts.Entity.Dtos.Le.description:
Earnings overview shape (skill §2 balance math). Returned by
`GET /v1/earnings/balance`.

StyleMint.Modules.Payouts.Entity.Dtos.Pa.description:
Customer-facing payout destination view. StyleMint.Modules.Payouts.Entity.Dtos.PayoutDestinationDto.AccountIdentifierMasked
shows only the last 4 chars of bank account numbers; PayPal /
eSewa identifiers (typically email-like) are masked at the local
part — "j****@example.com".

lines.description:
Optional summary of the earnings ledger window that funded
this payout. Empty when the bridge layer hasn't wired the
earnings-ledger lookup yet — the receipt still renders.

StyleMint.Modules.Payouts.Entity.Dtos.Pa.description:
§8J — printable invoice / receipt payload for a single payout.
Mobile client renders the actual PDF / share sheet from this DTO
(server-side PDF generation is a future `IPayoutInvoiceRenderer`
seam — Day-1 the structured payload is the contract). Header
fields freeze at issue time; ledger window snapshots the earnings
rows that funded this specific payout so the receipt reads as a
self-contained financial record.

StyleMint.Modules.Payouts.Enums.LedgerEn.description:
Reason an earnings_ledger row was written (skill §2). Negative-amount
kinds (PayoutDebit, FeeDebit) reduce the balance; positive kinds add
to it. Reversal rows mirror an original entry's kind and sign so a
SUM still nets out correctly.

Lifecycle of an earnings ledger row (skill §12). Pending → Settled
is the SOLE in-place mutation allowed on the ledger (skill §13.1);
every other correction is a new reversal row. Reversed marks the
effect "undone by a reversal row" — the original row keeps its
amount untouched so audit history stays intact.

StyleMint.Modules.Payouts.Enums.PayeeKin.description:
Two payee classes share the same ledger + payout engine (skill §1):
creators receive commissions on sourced sales, vendors receive net
proceeds. v2.0 amendments add courier as a third kind (Pillar B).

StyleMint.Modules.Payouts.Enums.PayoutDe.description:
Closed set of v1.1 payout destinations (CLAUDE.md §3 design-verified
invariant: NIMB / Laxmi / PayPal / eSewa). Skill §13.8 forbids
free-form bank support.

StyleMint.Modules.Payouts.Enums.PayoutMo.description:
How a payout was initiated (skill §5). AutomaticWeekly fires from
the Friday Hangfire batch (no fee, no minimum); OnDemand is a
customer-initiated withdrawal (2% fee, 10k-70k NPR bounds, 3-day
pending window).

StyleMint.Modules.Payouts.Enums.PayoutSt.description:
Payout lifecycle (skill §12). Requested rows are eligible for
customer-initiated cancellation; once Processing starts the
destination adapter has been engaged and cancellation requires
support intervention. Paid + Failed are terminal.
            
StyleMint.Modules.Payouts.Enums.PayoutState.Held (skill §6) is admin-only: a PayoutsOps moderator
pauses a Requested payout pending review; Release moves it back to
Requested so the weekly batch or executor can pick it up again.

StyleMint.Modules.Reach.Api.Controllers..description:
Mobile publish-panel response. One StyleMint.Modules.Reach.Api.Controllers.V1.ViewModels.PlatformConnection.PlatformConnectionsResponseVm.Platforms row per
external platform the orchestrator can publish to. Mobile renders:
<list type="bullet"><item>`IsConnected=true`, no `MissingScopes` → "Publish" CTA enabled.</item><item>`IsConnected=true`, non-empty `MissingScopes` → "Reconnect to grant scopes" CTA.</item><item>`IsConnected=false` → "Connect {Platform}" CTA.</item></list>

StyleMint.Modules.Reach.Entity.BoostBudg.description:
Mobile-friendly response shape for `GET /v1/reach/budgets/me`.
Returns 200 in both "creator has set a budget" and "creator has never
set one" cases so the client doesn't have to special-case a 404 as
an empty-state signal. StyleMint.Modules.Reach.Entity.BoostBudget.Dtos.BoostBudgetSnapshotDto.HasBudget drives the UI fork:
<list type="bullet"><item>`true`  → render the existing budget + spend</item><item>`false` → render the "Set your boost budget" flow</item></list>

retryAfterUtc.description:
When the target is in `RateLimited` state, the UTC instant

StyleMint.Shared.Core.Results.BulkResult.description:
Standardized response envelope for batch operations
(CSV imports, bulk fulfillment marks, batch creates, mass updates).
Per backend-core §12.6: the bulk OPERATION succeeds (returns
`ServiceResult.Ok(bulk)`) even when individual items fail.
`ServiceResult.Fail` is reserved for cases where the batch
couldn't start at all (empty input, oversize, malformed).
            
Items maintain their submitted index so the caller can correlate
per-row outcomes against the request payload without reshuffling.

StyleMint.Shared.Infrastructure.Core.Geo.description:
Where the coordinates on a shipping address came from. Stored alongside
lat/long so reviewers can tell "user pinned this on the map" from
"the geocoder guessed from the postal text" — they have very different
confidence profiles for delivery routing.

StyleMint.Shared.Infrastructure.Core.Ord.description:
Frozen address copy (skill §3). Decoupled from the live ShippingAddress
row in CartCheckout — the customer can edit / delete that row without
retroactively changing what was shipped.

StyleMint.Shared.Infrastructure.Core.Pay.description:
Closed set of v1.1 payment methods (skill stylemint-payments §1 + the
Style Mint design-verified invariant in CLAUDE.md §3). No Stripe, no
Khalti. Future PSPs add new values; existing values never shift.
            
Lives in Shared.Infrastructure so it can sit on the
StyleMint.Shared.Infrastructure.Core.Payments.IPaymentService contract that any module composes
against. `StyleMint.Modules.CartCheckout.Enums.PaymentMethod`
has identical values for historical reasons; the runtime cast
between the two is a no-op (same underlying ints).

Refund result echoed to the caller. StyleMint.Shared.Infrastructure.Core.Payments.RefundResult.State is the
string form of the RefundRecord state ("Pending" / "Completed" /
"Failed") so cross-module consumers don't depend on the Payments
module's enum type.
